# Photographic Composition as Large Systems

> Ongoing empirical research on photographic composition as a hierarchy of large interacting visual systems.

## Start here

- START_HERE.md — current research state and analysis order
- CORE_MODEL.md — current structural model
- TERMINOLOGY.md — project vocabulary
- FINDINGS.md — retained findings and pilot-specific observations
- FAILED_PATHS.md — rejected simplifications and confounds
- PILOT_INDEX.md — experiment history
- OPEN_QUESTIONS.md — unresolved research problems
- HOW_TO_CONTINUE_WITH_AN_LLM.md — continuation protocol for another model
- LLM_HANDOFF_COMPACT.md — compact single-file transfer package

## Machine-readable data

- machine/state.json
- machine/principles.json
- machine/terminology.json
- machine/experiments.jsonl

## Core idea

Do not begin photographic composition analysis with isolated placement rules.

Use this order:

1. identify the subject / frame goal;
2. segment the frame into large compositional systems;
3. analyze relations among those systems;
4. identify the subject-bearing system;
5. only then adjust subject reserve, local position, boundaries, crop, compensators, and other compromises.

Visual mass is treated as contextual rather than fixed.

## Important exclusions

Do not automatically reduce the project to:
- rule of thirds;
- golden ratio;
- generic leading-line advice;
- one universal subject-placement rule;
- one fixed visual-weight formula;
- centre-versus-boundary as a universal winner.
